title: Failures today, revenue later: the lag hypothesis
what: The Reactive Demand Index overlaid on Exponent's actual quarterly revenue, both rescaled to the same 100 = 2012-2019-average footing so they can share one axis honestly.
how: Exponent's revenue comes straight from its SEC filings. Use the shift buttons to slide the failure index forward in time: '+12 months' asks whether failure spikes line up with revenue roughly a year later, which is when lawsuits and formal investigations typically generate billable expert work.
thesis: If elevated failure activity in 2024-2025 shows up as Exponent revenue in 2025-2027, the current elevated index is effectively a backlog indicator - revenue strength that the market can't see in official filings yet.
caveats: This is a HYPOTHESIS you can eyeball, not a fitted statistical model - with only ~60 quarters of financial data, a regression would overstate certainty.
Both lines are indexed to their own average so they can share one axis; the overlay shows timing alignment, never magnitude.
